grammar.point: some / any with countable & uncountable nouns
grammar.point_ko: 셀 수 있는/없는 명사와 함께 쓰는 some / any
grammar.explanation_en: Use 'some' in positive sentences and offers ('I'd like some water', 'Would you like some bread?'). Use 'any' in negative sentences and questions ('I don't have any spoons', 'Do you have any tea?'). This rule applies to both countable and uncountable nouns.
grammar.explanation_ko: 긍정문과 권유문에는 'some'을 씁니다('I'd like some water', 'Would you like some bread?'). 부정문과 의문문에는 'any'를 씁니다('I don't have any spoons', 'Do you have any tea?'). 이 규칙은 셀 수 있는 명사와 없는 명사 모두에 적용됩니다.

examples.en: Could I have some water, please?
Do you have any vegetarian dishes?

reading.title: Dinner at a New Restaurant
reading.text: Yesterday, my friend and I tried a new restaurant. We didn't have a reservation, but there was some space. I ordered the spicy noodles, and my friend asked for something sweet. The food was delicious, but I didn't have any dessert because I was too full.
reading.text_ko: 어제 친구와 함께 새로운 식당을 가봤어요. 예약은 없었지만 자리가 좀 있었어요. 저는 매운 국수를 주문했고, 친구는 달콤한 것을 부탁했어요. 음식은 맛있었지만, 너무 배불러서 디저트는 안 먹었어요.

explanation.en: The text says 'We didn't have a reservation.'
The text says 'I ordered the spicy noodles.'
The text says 'because I was too full.'
